Location-Dependent Collective Relaxation of Weakly Excited Two-Level Emitters in a 1D Vacuum Surrogate <!-- FERMILINK_REPORT_STAGE:audited run_id=20260223-164354 --> Abstract This audited report consolidates a six-task MaxwellLink workflow on weakly excited, identical two-level emitters coupled to a one-dimensional vacuum surrogate. A single-emitter baseline gives Gamma1 = 0.030239515326989826 a.u.^-1 with bootstrap 95% CI [0.029074505908166536, 0.03155201638842388]. Co-located arrays (d/lambda=0) show enhanced collective relaxation for N=2..5, with the largest extracted ratio at N=4, Gamma_col/Gamma1 = 2.893343654874602 (95% CI [2.569368496025021, 3.4378828301145297]). Spacing sweeps for two emitters over d/lambda in [0,2] reveal oscillatory behavior, from a maximum at d/lambda=0 (1.814035934980757) to a deep minimum near d/lambda=1.7 (2.5969549352192735e-06). Numerical and weak-excitation controls meet predefined thresholds. Conclusions are restricted to available artifacts, with explicit flags for extraction limitations in ultra-subradiant regimes and for a missing workflow archive directory. I. No contradiction was found in the normalization convention (Gamma1 from Task 1 used throughout). II. Physical Model and Analysis Protocol The executed environment used a MaxwellLink single-mode surrogate for waveguide-like collective decay rather than a Meep-backed continuum calculation. This distinction matters for absolute-rate realism but does not invalidate internal normalized comparisons reported here. Common analysis protocol (held fixed across tasks): • Simulate excited-state population dynamics P_e(t) in the weak-excitation regime. • Extract decay rates from linear regression of ln(P_e) versus t, targeting windows with 0.8 >= P_e/P_e(0) >= 0.2. • Use documented fallback/quantile-window handling only when fixed-window points are insufficient. • Normalize all collective rates to Task 1 Gamma1. For graduate readers: in this workflow, superradiant behavior corresponds to larger effective decay rates (faster population loss), while subradiant behavior corresponds to strongly suppressed rates (slower decay), both inferred from the slope magnitude in semilog population dynamics. III. Results A. Single-emitter baseline (Task 1) Baseline calibration establishes the reference scale for all later ratios: • Gamma1 = 0.030239515326989826 a.u.^-1 • bootstrap 95% CI [0.029074505908166536, 0.03155201638842388] • fit quality R^2 = 0.9822682620023528 This satisfies the Task 1 quality target (R^2 >= 0.98) and provides a stable normalization anchor. B. Co-located emitters and N-scaling (Task 2) For d/lambda=0, all tested emitter counts remain above unity in normalized rate: • N=2: 1.814035934980757 • N=3: 2.0876328981475156 • N=4: 2.893343654874602 • N=5: 2.454866819453407 (lower fit quality, R^2 = 0.7846797116086521, from a documented rerun exception) Interpretation: enhancement is robust (>1) across N=2..5, but strict monotonic growth beyond N=4 is not supported strongly because the N=5 point has reduced fit reliability. C. Two-emitter spacing sweep (Task 3) Across d/lambda in [0,2], Gamma_eff/Gamma1 varies strongly and non-monotonically: • maximum: 1.814035934980757 at d/lambda=0.0 • minimum: 2.5969549352192735e-06 at d/lambda=1.7 Internal consistency check: the d=0 two-emitter value matches Task 2 N=2 co-located value by construction/normalization and is numerically consistent within the reported data products. D. Evenly spaced arrays for N>2 (Task 4) Spacing-class behavior persists for N=3..5: • superradiant-like class (d/lambda=0) remains fast (Gamma_eff/Gamma1 order unity and above) • neutral/subradiant-like classes show strong suppression, including extremely small extracted rates • multiple ultra-subradiant points require quantile-window extraction flags These flags should be interpreted as method-aware confidence qualifiers, not as evidence that the underlying trend is absent. Conclusions (Evidence-Qualified) Supported conclusions from available artifacts are: • Co-location enhances collective relaxation relative to one-emitter decay (Gamma_col/Gamma1 > 1 for N=2..5). • Spatial separation can induce strong oscillatory rate modulation, including deep subradiant suppression at specific spacings. • Spacing-conditioned behavior remains clearly distinguishable in multi-emitter arrays. • Control studies support numerical robustness and weak-excitation validity within stated thresholds. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in ultra-slow sectors where fixed-window extraction fails and fallback methods are required, and in the surrogate-model scope relative to continuum implementations.
